items_missed: No agenda statement at all — never laid out the roadmap, never gave the 10-15 minute timeframe, never asked for confirmation. The call opened straight into 'how may I help you' and stayed reactive the whole way.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any version of it — went straight to transactional lookup on an inbound call.

Save Your Ass prep speech completely absent. This is a 20-tote, one-picture, one-mirror move billed against a 2.5-hour minimum — staging totes by the door is exactly the coaching that protects the customer's bill.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. The move includes a mirror and framed pictures — the two most damage-prone items on the truck — and the customer got zero coverage explanation.

Meet Your Mover never pitched. He described the movers' day-of ETA call ('our movers they do give you a call whenever they're headed your direction'), which is not the same thing and doesn't earn the credit.
Never asked about stairs or floors at either the pickup house or the drop-off house — only asked what floor the storage unit was on.
Never asked about walk distance at any of the three locations, including a self-storage facility where the unit-to-truck walk is often the longest part of the job.
Clock mechanics half-explained: stated the 2.5-hour minimum but never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never explained 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum.
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — he covered no trip fee and no deposit but skipped no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees.
Never asked about packing needs, garage/attic/patio rooms, or 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?'
Collected the customer's name (Norman Allen) and then never used it once — called him 'boss' five times instead.
No hours of operation or callback instructions given before hanging up.
Customer had to ask 'what's the name of your company again? I'm sorry' at minute 9, and the reply came back garbled — a clarity problem, not a customer problem.
Made the customer repeat the home size because he hadn't read the existing profile before asking.
top_strength: The On-Time Guarantee explanation was the best moment on the call and genuinely above average. Hector volunteered the two-hour arrival window unprompted for a 2:30 afternoon slot, explained honestly why it exists ('we are at the mercy of how well the pace of the move that scheduled before yours'), gave the exact window (1:30 to 3:30), covered both directions of the variance, and then landed the guarantee with real numbers — '$50 and then... a continuation every thirty minutes afterwards.' He also showed his estimate math out loud segment by segment (an hour to load, thirty minutes to the storage drop and drive, an hour at the last stop) so the customer could see how the 2.5-hour minimum was derived rather than just being handed a number.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: run the Save Your Ass prep speech on every call, including the small ones — especially the small ones. This move is 20 totes, a picture and a mirror against a 2.5-hour minimum, which means prep is the entire difference between paying the minimum and paying overage. The language: 'Norman, one thing that saves people real money — anything you can stage by the front door before we get there, or throw in the car yourself, comes straight off the clock. Totes lined up in one room instead of spread across the house can knock thirty minutes off the bill. Does that make sense?' Second priority: he never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage on a move whose entire inventory is a mirror and framed pictures. That is the single item on this job most likely to break, and the customer hung up not knowing there is $2,000 of coverage behind it — say it every time, right after the hourly rate. Third, and this is the cheap one: he asked for Norman's first and last name, wrote it down, and then said 'boss' five times. Use the name — it costs nothing and it is three of the eleven points he lost outside pricing. Finally, open with an actual agenda. 'I'll grab a few details about your move, then walk you through pricing — takes about ten minutes. Sound good?' takes eight seconds and it is a free seven-point section he scored 4 on.
phone_presence_notes: Energetic and friendly in filler ('cool cool cool', 'no worries', 'boss') and he apologized graciously for making the customer repeat himself, but there was no name use, no rapport moment, and the customer stayed monosyllabic ('Okay.' 'Correct.' 'Yeah.') from start to finish.
audio_review_reason: Transcript contains garbled rep speech ('Was like you sure you're calling the right present non plan we are Einstein Moving Company') and the customer asked which company he had reached nine minutes in — pull the audio to check whether this is a transcription artifact or a real diction/pace problem.
